facts.label: Identity and perimeter
facts.text: - Issuer and reporting entity: Brightstar Lottery PLC (the "Parent") with its consolidated subsidiaries. The annual report states "In July 2025, the Parent changed its corporate name from International Game Technology PLC to Brightstar Lottery PLC (NYSE: BRSL)" (20-F page:4). The pack file names still carry "igt", which is the earlier name, and identity rests on the text, not the filename. - Basis: US GAAP, single operating segment. The interim report states "The Company operates and manages its continuing operations business as a single segment" (second-quarter 2026 interim report page:10). - Perimeter change: the gaming and digital business was sold on July 1, 2025 and is shown as discontinued operations ("On July 1, 2025, the Company completed the sale of the Gaming & Digital business", interim report page:7). Continuing-operations figures for 2025 comparatives therefore exclude that business, and discontinued-operations amounts are separate lines. The annual report, the 2025 nine-month report and the 2026 reports must not be mixed without the discontinued-operations label. - Non-controlling interests: the Italian Lotto license is held through a consortium that Brightstar leads ("a consortium comprised of Allwyn, Arianna 2001, Novomatic Italia, and led by Brightstar", interim report page:12). The income statement and equity statement show non-controlling interests ("Non-controlling interests 1,173 715", interim report page:4), so consolidated cash, debt and EBITDA include partner interests. The ownership percentage of the consortium is not located in the filing text; the Q1 2026 deck gives "BRSL share €879M or $1.03B" of the final installment (Q1 deck page:6), which is a management claim. - Debt roles: the annual report's debt note lists issuers as Parent, Brightstar Lottery Holdings B.V. and "Parent/Brightstar Global Solutions Corporation" for the 2033 notes (20-F page:169). The paragraph below the table names the co-issuer "Brightstar Lottery Global Solutions Corporation". These two spellings are a naming conflict inside one source and need one resolution downstream. Term loan borrower: Brightstar Lottery S.p.A. (20-F page:171). Guarantors are described only as "certain of the Parent’s subsidiaries"; no list of named guarantors is in the pack. Restricted and unrestricted group distinctions are not described in the supplied text.

facts.label: Financial statements and notes
facts.text: - Annual report: audited consolidated balance sheet, operations, comprehensive income, cash flows and equity statements, with PwC opinion on statements and internal control ("In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material respects", 20-F page:134). Debt note 15 is at 20-F pages:168-176, liquidity at pages:56-57, and cash requirements at page:59. - Interim reports: unaudited, "do not include all of the information and note disclosures required by GAAP for complete financial statements" (interim report page:8). Each has balance sheet, operations, cash flows, equity statement, debt note, interest expense note, commitments and management discussion. - Debt coverage: the June 30, 2026 debt table lists each note and facility with principal, issuance cost and carrying amount, and a maturity table by currency (interim report page:14: "Total principal amounts 1,500 2,883 4,383"). The December 31, 2025 equivalent is in the annual report (20-F page:168). The March 2026 revolving facility refinancing is described in the interim report at page:15 ("entered into a senior secured multicurrency revolving credit facilities agreement expiring March 2031"). - Liquidity coverage: "Total Liquidity 1,742 3,036" for June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025 (interim report page:27). The figure is built from revolver availability plus cash. - Cash-paid interest and tax: "Interest paid 68 89" and "Income taxes paid 16 32" for six months (interim report page:6). - Commitments: the Italian Lotto installments are in the interim report ("On April 24, 2026, LottoItalia paid the final installment", page:12); unconditional purchase obligations at December 31, 2025 are in the annual report (page:59). Factoring is disclosed in the interim report at page:12. Finance lease right-of-use assets are shown in the other assets note (page:12); operating lease liabilities appear only as a balance sheet line (page:3), and no lease maturity schedule or finance lease liability is located in the interim report text read (searched for "lease liabilit" and "finance lease"). The annual report carries the lease notes (20-F pages:162-166).

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is complete enough for the downstream credit work, with three restrictions. First, the reported picture is a company that has just paid a very large one-off cash item: the final Italian Lotto license installment of $1,675 million in April 2026, which turned six-month operating cash flow to a $1,174 million outflow and lifted net debt from $2,732 million to $3,796 million between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026. Net debt leverage on management's definition moved from 2.44x to 3.24x, and the December 2025 figure sat beside a $1,680 million payable to the Italian regulator that was outside debt. Second, the leverage and cover ratios rest on Adjusted EBITDA, a management non-GAAP measure that adds back amortization of upfront license fees, and the filings supply no covenant thresholds against which to judge headroom. Third, the capital structure is mainly senior secured, mixed in currency, with about two thirds of principal in euros, and cash distributions to non-controlling interests are a recurring claim on consolidated cash flow. Liquidity of $1,742 million and a first maturity of $228 million in 2027 give near-term room, but the evidence ends at the August 4, 2026 interim report.

facts.label: Debt instruments and security
facts.text: By currency at June 30, 2026, principal is 1,500 dollar-denominated and 2,883 euro-denominated, together 4,383 (Q2 6-K page:14, "Total principal amounts 1,500 2,883 4,383"). The December 31, 2025 principal of the January 2027 term loan is 235 long-term plus 118 current. Notes are secured by "the shares of Brightstar Lottery S.p.A., certain intercompany loans with principal balances in excess of $10 million, and certain accounts receivable" (20-F page:169). The Q2 6-K says the revolver obligations are guaranteed "subject to agreed guarantor coverage thresholds based on consolidated assets and adjusted EBITDA" (Q2 6-K page:15); the guarantors are not named. Debt is described as all senior secured; no unsecured or subordinated debt, and no structurally separate unrestricted group, appears in the debt note.

facts.label: Covenants and restrictions
facts.text: The revolver agreement "contains a maximum net leverage ratio covenant and a minimum interest coverage ratio covenant" (Q2 6-K page:15) and the borrowers "were in compliance with such covenants" at June 30, 2026 (Q2 6-K page:27). No threshold, step-down, covenant EBITDA definition or reported covenant ratio is printed, so headroom is Not calculable. The term loan agreements at December 31, 2025 limited dividends and share repurchases to "$400 million if any two" ratings are below Ba1/BB+ and $550 million if two are at or above that level, with the cap removed if two ratings are at or above Baa3/BBB- (20-F page:171); the ratings at that date were BBB- (Fitch), Ba1 (Moody's) and BB+ (S&P) (20-F page:168). In March 2026 the company amended certain provisions of the 2030 term loans "to align such provisions under the RCF Agreement" (Q2 6-K page:15) and the amended text is not supplied, so the current distribution cap cannot be stated.

facts.label: Data quality and conflicts
facts.text: - Net debt at December 31, 2025: the filing-derived figure is 2,732 (4,178 less 1,446); the Q4 deck prints "4,777 2,723 FY'24 FY'25" (Q4 deck page:6). The 9 difference does not change the printed 2.4x. The filing-derived figure is used. - The final Lotto installment appears as 1,680 (payable at December 31, 2025), $1.68B (Q4 deck), $1.67B (Q1 deck and Q2 deck) and 1,675 (cash paid). The balance sheet and cash flow figures are each used for their own date; the filing does not state the translation bridge. - The euro notes and term loans are translated at period-end rates that differ by date (the principal of the same euro term loans reads 1,175, 1,150 and 1,139 at December 31, 2025, March 31, 2026 and June 30, 2026), so dollar debt moves with the exchange rate without any repayment. - Printed liquidity of 1,742 equals the revolver availability plus cash within rounding (1,743 summed). The printed 1,185 reconciles to $650 million plus the euro facility less 604 drawn only if the euro term loan principal of 1,139 is read as the dollar value of 1.0 billion euros; this is an inference from the 20-F repayment schedule of 200, 200, 200 and 400 million euros and is not stated in the Q2 6-K. - The 20-F debt note names the 5.750% notes co-issuer "Brightstar Global Solutions Corporation" in its table and "Brightstar Lottery Global Solutions Corporation" in its text (20-F page:169); the debt table here carries both spellings. - Where this module goes beyond the readiness handoff: the readiness handoff said period-end euro rates were not located; the implied rate for June 30, 2026 can be inferred from the euro term loan principal, as noted above. It also said whether letters of credit reduce the new revolver was unstated; that remains unstated, and the inferred reconciliation of 1,185 suggests no deduction but is not proof.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The business is a contracted, wager-linked lottery services company whose creditor-relevant features sit in four places. First, revenue visibility is high on paper, with about 92% of FY2025 revenue from long-term operating, facilities management and lottery management contracts, but U.S. contracts can be ended by the lottery authority at will with limited notice and the two Italian licenses together supplied about 37% of revenue. Second, the Italian licenses are the key transaction exposure: the new nine-year Lotto license cost an upfront fee of €2,230 million, paid in three installments ending April 24, 2026, and it is now amortized against revenue; the Scratch and Win license expires in September 2028. Third, control is concentrated in De Agostini with 63.28% of votes, and the documented behaviour since the sale of the gaming business on July 1, 2025 is debt reduction alongside large shareholder distributions, within term loan limits whose current text is not supplied. Fourth, the Italian Lotto structure shares cash flow with partners, so consolidated figures include cash that belongs partly to non-controlling interests. The evidence is adequate for a business-context fact pack, but the concession terms, the consortium agreements and any event after August 4, 2026 are not in the pack.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Sale of the gaming and digital business. On July 1, 2025 the company completed the sale of IGT Gaming to a holding company owned by funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management, pursuant to agreements entered into on July 26, 2024. The 20-F records total consideration, net of $134 million of cash and restricted cash transferred, of $4.1 billion and a pre-tax gain of $112 million (20-F page:156). The business is a discontinued operation, so every continuing-operations comparative excludes it. Continuing involvement is limited to licensing between the two groups, a 60.0% interest in Rhode Island VLT Company LLC whose economic benefits were transferred to IGT Gaming, and a guarantee of a lease of IGT Gaming that expires September 30, 2032 with maximum base-rent exposure of $94 million at June 30, 2026 (Q2 6-K page:17 and page:18). A receivable from the buyer of $21 million at June 30, 2026 will be collected through 2027 (Q2 6-K page:17). De Agostini retained an investment in the combined private company (20-F page:156); its size is not stated in the text read.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Use of proceeds. The filings state two uses. First, debt repayment: on the sale the company redeemed the 4.125% dollar notes due April 2026 and the 3.500% euro notes due June 2026 and prepaid euro term loan and revolver amounts, and the interim notes say $2 billion of debt was required to be repaid within six months of closing (20-F page:170; Q2 6-K page:17). Second, shareholder returns: the 20-F describes a "previously announced plan to return $1.1 billion of net cash proceeds from the IGT Gaming divestiture to shareholders" (20-F page:58). Execution documented in FY2025 includes a special dividend of $600 million (Q4 deck page:6, management claim), a $250 million accelerated share repurchase and a total of $770 million of cash dividends and $271 million of repurchases for the year (20-F page:123 and page:139).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Italian Lotto license. On July 16, 2025 the regulator notified that the consortium led by Brightstar had been awarded the Italian Lotto license for nine years from December 1, 2025. The upfront fee was €2,230 million, paid as €500 million on July 17, 2025, €300 million on November 28, 2025 and €1,430 million ($1,675 million) on April 24, 2026 (20-F page:163; Q2 6-K page:12). The Q1 deck states Brightstar's share of the final installment as €879 million or $1.03 billion (Q1 deck page:6, management claim); that share equals about 61.5% of €1,430 million, consistent with the stated ownership of Lottoitalia. Partners funded their share through non-controlling interest capital increases of $650 million in the first half of 2026 (Q2 6-K page:5). The license is amortized against revenue from December 2025 and the Q2 deck states that about $175 million of incremental Lotto-related service revenue amortization affects FY2026 reported growth (Q2 deck page:7, management claim).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt issues and refinancing. In September 2024 Brightstar Lottery Holdings B.V. issued €500 million of 4.250% notes at par (20-F page:170). In March 2025 the Parent and Brightstar Lottery S.p.A. entered into a facilities agreement for two €500 million term loans due September 2030, one used to repay revolver borrowings and one to fund the share of the Lotto fee (20-F page:171). In December 2025 the Parent and a subsidiary as co-issuers issued $750 million of 5.750% senior secured notes due January 2033 at par and used the proceeds and cash to redeem the $750 million 6.250% notes due January 2027 at 101.22%, with a $10 million loss on extinguishment (20-F page:169 and page:170). In March 2026 the company signed new senior secured revolving credit facilities of $650 million and €1.0 billion expiring March 2031, effective April 2026, cancelled both revolvers due July 2027 and amended the 2030 term loans to align provisions; in April 2026 it prepaid the remaining €200 million of the January 2027 term loan from revolver borrowings (Q2 6-K page:15). The June 30, 2026 principal is $4,383 million with the first maturity of $228 million in 2027 (see the financial base). Documented status of all items above: completed. No debt issuance is documented after June 30, 2026.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Brightstar Lottery PLC has an adequate fundamental credit profile with real near-term support but limited margin for error. The strongest support is contracted, wager-linked revenue, about 92% of FY2025 revenue, and liquidity of USD 1,742 million with no debt maturing before 2027, after the final USD 1,675 million Italian Lotto payment was absorbed. The weakest point is the quality of 3.24x net leverage: it uses management's Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back USD 323 million of license amortization and would read 4.48x without it, while partners and a controlling shareholder take part of the cash flow. The outcome depends on free cash flow after the investment cycle, the Scratch and Win renewal in September 2028 beside USD 798 million of 2028 maturities, and covenant terms that are not supplied.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Net leverage is acceptable on management's measure but weaker on a cash-oriented one. Net debt was USD 3,796 million at June 30, 2026 against last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,170 million, which is 3.24x, and total debt over the same EBITDA is 3.72x [financial base: leverage]. Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 323 million of license-fee amortization for the same period, and without that add-back net leverage is 4.48x [financial base: definition review]. The add-back relates to fees already paid in cash, which is why the reported figure is not unreasonable, but it means the leverage ratio flatters the cash burden of renewals in a business whose Italian licenses run for about nine years. The headline rise from 2.44x at December 31, 2025 to 3.24x mostly reflects the settlement of a USD 1,680 million regulator payable that sat outside debt; counting that payable, leverage at December 31, 2025 would have been 3.94x, so the like-for-like movement over six months was a decrease, helped by USD 650 million of partner capital contributions [financial base: claims outside debt; business context: Italian Lotto license].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity and maturities are comfortable for two years and heavier after that. Liquidity is USD 1,742 million, made of USD 558 million of cash and USD 1,185 million of undrawn revolver, against 2027 and 2028 principal maturities of USD 1,026 million combined, which is 1.70x cover [financial base: liquidity and maturities]. Total principal is USD 4,383 million, of which USD 2,883 million is in euros and all of it is senior secured, and the 2028 to 2030 maturities total USD 2,801 million, about 64% of principal. The new revolver runs to March 2031 with USD 604 million drawn. The risk is a concentrated refinancing window in 2028 to 2030 that coincides with the Scratch and Win renewal.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Cash generation is positive before license payments but is shared. Operating cash flow excluding Lotto payments was USD 761 million over the last twelve months and free cash flow excluding them USD 387 million; reported free cash flow was negative USD 2,214 million because of the USD 2,601 million of license payments in the period [financial base: financials]. Out of the USD 387 million, partners took USD 163 million of distributions, leaving USD 224 million for debt reduction and shareholders, and shareholder returns of USD 1,090 million over the same twelve months (including the USD 600 million special dividend funded from the sale of the gaming business) therefore came from sale proceeds and not from recurring cash flow [business context: ownership and governance]. In the first half of 2026 free cash flow excluding Lotto payments of USD 269 million less partner distributions of USD 163 million was USD 106 million, below the USD 130 million returned to shareholders. Capital expenditure of USD 190 million is expected in the second half of 2026 for new contracts.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The business has strong contractual visibility, concentrated in Italy and exposed to renewals. About 92% of revenue comes from long-term contracts, but the two Italian licenses supplied about 37% of FY2025 revenue and many U.S. contracts can be ended at will with limited notice [business context: operating model]. The Italian Lotto license runs to November 2034, while the Scratch and Win license expires in September 2028 and is not renewable unless its terms say so; the new Lotto license required an upfront fee of EUR 2,230 million. If a renewal needs a comparable upfront payment, it would arrive when USD 798 million of debt matures, a mechanic and not a forecast, since the renewal terms are not in the evidence.

De Agostini holds 46.29% of the shares and 63.28% of the votes, so distribution and leverage policy is its to set; the term loan agreements limited distributions at December 31, 2025, but the March 2026 amendment is not supplied.

facts.label: Evidence trace view
facts.text: The analysis is traceable enough for a draft snapshot, with five minor defects and no material or critical one. Of 130 quoted spans in the three handoffs that quote the sources, every span was found in the pinned sources, and one locator pointed to the wrong page; every derived ratio was recomputed from its inputs and matched. The strongest support is that leverage inputs, liquidity, maturities and ownership come from filed statements. The weakest point is that Adjusted EBITDA, net debt and net debt leverage come only from management presentations. What decides committee use is whether covenant levels, license agreements and any filing after August 4, 2026 can be obtained, because the renewal, distribution-cap and covenant-headroom conclusions cannot be traced without them.

### Readiness view

The effective source set supports the requested work with limitations, so every selected consumer is assessed as ready with limitations and none as conditional or blocked. The assertion is source sufficiency only. Whether the later modules accept their inputs is not evaluated here. The audited annual report and the three interim reports give the statements, debt note, maturity table, liquidity table and commitments needed for a financial data build. The business and transaction work has the annual report's business description and the interim notes on the sale of the gaming business and the Italian Lotto license. The principal restrictions are the absence of any report after the August 2026 interim filing, the absence of covenant levels and debt documents, and the reliance on slide decks for Adjusted EBITDA and leverage.
### Source-by-source assessment
#### Identity and perimeter

- Issuer and reporting entity: Brightstar Lottery PLC (the "Parent") with its consolidated subsidiaries. The annual report states "In July 2025, the Parent changed its corporate name from International Game Technology PLC to Brightstar Lottery PLC (NYSE: BRSL)" (20-F page:4). The pack file names still carry "igt", which is the earlier name, and identity rests on the text, not the filename.

- Basis: US GAAP, single operating segment. The interim report states "The Company operates and manages its continuing operations business as a single segment" (second-quarter 2026 interim report page:10).

- Perimeter change: the gaming and digital business was sold on July 1, 2025 and is shown as discontinued operations ("On July 1, 2025, the Company completed the sale of the Gaming & Digital business", interim report page:7). Continuing-operations figures for 2025 comparatives therefore exclude that business, and discontinued-operations amounts are separate lines. The annual report, the 2025 nine-month report and the 2026 reports must not be mixed without the discontinued-operations label.

- Non-controlling interests: the Italian Lotto license is held through a consortium that Brightstar leads ("a consortium comprised of Allwyn, Arianna 2001, Novomatic Italia, and led by Brightstar", interim report page:12). The income statement and equity statement show non-controlling interests ("Non-controlling interests 1,173 715", interim report page:4), so consolidated cash, debt and EBITDA include partner interests. The ownership percentage of the consortium is not located in the filing text; the Q1 2026 deck gives "BRSL share €879M or $1.03B" of the final installment (Q1 deck page:6), which is a management claim.

- Debt roles: the annual report's debt note lists issuers as Parent, Brightstar Lottery Holdings B.V. and "Parent/Brightstar Global Solutions Corporation" for the 2033 notes (20-F page:169). The paragraph below the table names the co-issuer "Brightstar Lottery Global Solutions Corporation". These two spellings are a naming conflict inside one source and need one resolution downstream. Term loan borrower: Brightstar Lottery S.p.A. (20-F page:171). Guarantors are described only as "certain of the Parent’s subsidiaries"; no list of named guarantors is in the pack. Restricted and unrestricted group distinctions are not described in the supplied text.
#### Financial statements and notes

- Annual report: audited consolidated balance sheet, operations, comprehensive income, cash flows and equity statements, with PwC opinion on statements and internal control ("In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material respects", 20-F page:134). Debt note 15 is at 20-F pages:168-176, liquidity at pages:56-57, and cash requirements at page:59.

- Interim reports: unaudited, "do not include all of the information and note disclosures required by GAAP for complete financial statements" (interim report page:8). Each has balance sheet, operations, cash flows, equity statement, debt note, interest expense note, commitments and management discussion.

- Debt coverage: the June 30, 2026 debt table lists each note and facility with principal, issuance cost and carrying amount, and a maturity table by currency (interim report page:14: "Total principal amounts 1,500 2,883 4,383"). The December 31, 2025 equivalent is in the annual report (20-F page:168). The March 2026 revolving facility refinancing is described in the interim report at page:15 ("entered into a senior secured multicurrency revolving credit facilities agreement expiring March 2031").
- Liquidity coverage: "Total Liquidity 1,742 3,036" for June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025 (interim report page:27). The figure is built from revolver availability plus cash.
- Cash-paid interest and tax: "Interest paid 68 89" and "Income taxes paid 16 32" for six months (interim report page:6).

- Commitments: the Italian Lotto installments are in the interim report ("On April 24, 2026, LottoItalia paid the final installment", page:12); unconditional purchase obligations at December 31, 2025 are in the annual report (page:59). Factoring is disclosed in the interim report at page:12. Finance lease right-of-use assets are shown in the other assets note (page:12); operating lease liabilities appear only as a balance sheet line (page:3), and no lease maturity schedule or finance lease liability is located in the interim report text read (searched for "lease liabilit" and "finance lease"). The annual report carries the lease notes (20-F pages:162-166).
#### Earnings presentations

- The three decks contain the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, net debt leverage, free cash flow, outlook and same-store sales. Example: "Net debt leverage* 3.24x" appears on the Q2 2026 deck (page:6) and "Adjusted EBITDA 286 274" in its reconciliation (page:10). FY2025 "Adjusted EBITDA 304 290 1,121 1,170" is in the Q4 deck reconciliation (Q4 deck page:8). They are issuer presentations, so they provide attributed supporting claims. The decks themselves say the non-GAAP measures are defined by the company ("other companies may define non-GAAP measures differently", Q2 deck page:3).

- Adjusted EBITDA, net debt and net debt leverage are not in any filed statement in this pack. A search of the annual report and the three interim reports for "Adjusted EBITDA" and "AEBITDA" finds the annual report only in compensation-plan and definition text (20-F pages:5, 73, 74, 75, 184), and finds nothing in the three interim reports. This is a source-quality limit, not a missing document.

- Extraction fidelity: the decks are slide images converted to text. The extraction merges several slides per chunk and loses chart structure; the maturity chart on the Q2 deck (page:6) is a string of numbers without axis labels. No chart or image was inspected, and speaker notes are not claimed. The slide-by-slide coverage cannot be accounted for and is a parse gap. The filed debt tables control instead.
#### Version and conflict observations (preserved, not reconciled)

- Italian Lotto final installment, translated amount: the December 31, 2025 balance sheet shows "Payable to ADM 6 — 1,680" (interim report page:3 shows the 1,680 payable), the Q4 deck says "€1.43B or $1.68B due in Q2’26", the Q1 and Q2 decks say "$1.67B", and the cash flow statement shows "Italian Lotto License payment (1,675)" (interim report page:5). The difference is consistent with euro translation at different dates but the filing does not state it as a reconciliation; downstream modules must use the cash-flow amount for the payment and the balance-sheet amount for the December 2025 liability, each labelled.

- Leverage bases: the Q1 deck states "Q1’26 Net debt leverage* 2.4x; ~3.5x pro forma for final Lotto license payment" while the Q2 deck states 3.24x at Q2 2026. These are different dates and one is pro forma; they are not a restatement.

- Revolving facilities: two facilities due July 2027 were cancelled and replaced in March 2026 (interim report page:15), so the annual report's facility table (20-F page:173) is superseded for revolver terms. Both documents stay active as separate dated sources.

- Liquidity arithmetic: the printed components at June 30, 2026 are 1,185 and 558 against a printed total of 1,742; the page footnote says amounts may not foot due to rounding (interim report page:8).

- Letters of credit: the annual report states "There were no letters of credit outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facilities" at December 31, 2025 (20-F page:176). The June 30, 2026 interim report mentions a letter of credit only for the guarantee of the sold business's lease (page:18); whether any letters of credit sit on the new revolver at June 30, 2026 is not stated in the text read.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Reported net debt leverage is 3.24x at June 30, 2026 after the final Italian Lotto license payment, up from 2.44x at December 31, 2025. Liquidity is $1,742 million and no debt matures before 2027. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure, covenant levels are not supplied, and nothing after August 4, 2026 is covered. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The $1,675 million final license payment in April 2026 drove six-month operating cash flow to a $1,174 million outflow. | Free cash flow is negative on a reported basis; the year-end leverage of 2.44x did not reflect the $1,680 million payable. | High |

| Total debt at June 30, 2026 is $4,383 million principal, of which $2,883 million is euro-denominated; maturities start with $228 million in 2027. | Currency moves change dollar debt, and each 2028 to 2030 maturity is at least $798 million. | High |

| Adjusted EBITDA of $1,170 million for the last twelve months adds back $323 million of license-fee amortization. | Without that add-back, net debt leverage would be 4.48x, so the add-back drives the reported leverage. | Medium |

| Interest cover on cash interest is 6.09x for the last twelve months, against 5.26x for FY2025. | Cover is adequate on the management measure, but non-controlling interests take $163 million of cash distributions a year. | Medium |

| Liquidity is $558 million cash plus $1,185 million undrawn revolver, down from $3,036 million at December 31, 2025. | The Lotto payment consumed most of the cash buffer; the revolver now carries $604 million drawn. | High |
### Financial base view

The financial base is complete enough for the downstream credit work, with three restrictions. First, the reported picture is a company that has just paid a very large one-off cash item: the final Italian Lotto license installment of $1,675 million in April 2026, which turned six-month operating cash flow to a $1,174 million outflow and lifted net debt from $2,732 million to $3,796 million between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026. Net debt leverage on management's definition moved from 2.44x to 3.24x, and the December 2025 figure sat beside a $1,680 million payable to the Italian regulator that was outside debt. Second, the leverage and cover ratios rest on Adjusted EBITDA, a management non-GAAP measure that adds back amortization of upfront license fees, and the filings supply no covenant thresholds against which to judge headroom. Third, the capital structure is mainly senior secured, mixed in currency, with about two thirds of principal in euros, and cash distributions to non-controlling interests are a recurring claim on consolidated cash flow. Liquidity of $1,742 million and a first maturity of $228 million in 2027 give near-term room, but the evidence ends at the August 4, 2026 interim report.

### Covenants and restrictions

The revolver agreement "contains a maximum net leverage ratio covenant and a minimum interest coverage ratio covenant" (Q2 6-K page:15) and the borrowers "were in compliance with such covenants" at June 30, 2026 (Q2 6-K page:27). No threshold, step-down, covenant EBITDA definition or reported covenant ratio is printed, so headroom is Not calculable. The term loan agreements at December 31, 2025 limited dividends and share repurchases to "$400 million if any two" ratings are below Ba1/BB+ and $550 million if two are at or above that level, with the cap removed if two ratings are at or above Baa3/BBB- (20-F page:171); the ratings at that date were BBB- (Fitch), Ba1 (Moody's) and BB+ (S&P) (20-F page:168). In March 2026 the company amended certain provisions of the 2030 term loans "to align such provisions under the RCF Agreement" (Q2 6-K page:15) and the amended text is not supplied, so the current distribution cap cannot be stated.
### Definition and sensitivity review
| Measure | FY2025 | LTM June 30, 2026 | Basis |
| Management Adjusted EBITDA | 1,121 | 1,170 | Adds back foreign exchange, restructuring, stock-based compensation, other expense and amortization of upfront license fees |
| Less license-fee amortization add-back | 898 | 847 | Calculated: 1,121 - 223 and 1,170 - 323 |
| Net debt / EBITDA after removing that add-back | 3.04x | 4.48x | Calculated: 2,732 / 898 and 3,796 / 847 |
| EBITDA after removing that add-back / cash interest | 4.22x | 4.41x | Calculated: 898 / 213 and 847 / 192 |
| Net debt including the Italian regulator payable / Adjusted EBITDA | 3.94x | Not applicable | Calculated: (2,732 + 1,680) / 1,121; the payable was settled in 2026 |
| Net debt including lease liabilities / Adjusted EBITDA | 2.55x | Not supplied | Calculated: (2,732 + 121) / 1,121; June 30, 2026 lease liabilities not located |

| Net debt / (Adjusted EBITDA less non-controlling interest distributions) | Not applicable | 3.77x | Calculated: 3,796 / (1,170 - 163) using H1 2026 distributions of 163 as the LTM figure; both sides are 100% consolidated |

These are analyst sensitivities, not reported metrics and not covenant calculations. Amortization of upfront license fees is a non-cash reduction of revenue that arises from fees already paid in cash (926 in FY2025 and 1,675 in H1 2026); adding it back is management's convention.
### Data quality and conflicts

- Net debt at December 31, 2025: the filing-derived figure is 2,732 (4,178 less 1,446); the Q4 deck prints "4,777 2,723 FY'24 FY'25" (Q4 deck page:6). The 9 difference does not change the printed 2.4x. The filing-derived figure is used.

- The final Lotto installment appears as 1,680 (payable at December 31, 2025), $1.68B (Q4 deck), $1.67B (Q1 deck and Q2 deck) and 1,675 (cash paid). The balance sheet and cash flow figures are each used for their own date; the filing does not state the translation bridge.

- The euro notes and term loans are translated at period-end rates that differ by date (the principal of the same euro term loans reads 1,175, 1,150 and 1,139 at December 31, 2025, March 31, 2026 and June 30, 2026), so dollar debt moves with the exchange rate without any repayment.

- Printed liquidity of 1,742 equals the revolver availability plus cash within rounding (1,743 summed). The printed 1,185 reconciles to $650 million plus the euro facility less 604 drawn only if the euro term loan principal of 1,139 is read as the dollar value of 1.0 billion euros; this is an inference from the 20-F repayment schedule of 200, 200, 200 and 400 million euros and is not stated in the Q2 6-K.

- The 20-F debt note names the 5.750% notes co-issuer "Brightstar Global Solutions Corporation" in its table and "Brightstar Lottery Global Solutions Corporation" in its text (20-F page:169); the debt table here carries both spellings.

- Where this module goes beyond the readiness handoff: the readiness handoff said period-end euro rates were not located; the implied rate for June 30, 2026 can be inferred from the euro term loan principal, as noted above. It also said whether letters of credit reduce the new revolver was unstated; that remains unstated, and the inferred reconciliation of 1,185 suggests no deduction but is not proof.
### Subsequent events and outlook

- After June 30, 2026 and before the August 4, 2026 report: a dividend of $0.23 per share, about 42 in total, declared July 30, 2026 and payable September 1, 2026 (Q2 6-K page:18); repurchases of 0.9 million shares for $10 million through July 31, 2026 (Q2 6-K page:19); payment of the Mexican tax settlement on July 10, 2026, amount not stated (Q2 6-K page:17).

- Management outlook for FY2026 (deck claims): revenue $2.50B to $2.55B, Adjusted EBITDA $1.16B to $1.19B, capex about $450M to $475M (Q2 deck page:7). These are forward-looking management statements, not evidence of results.
- Not supplied: any filing after August 4, 2026, including a third-quarter 2026 report; ratings after December 31, 2025.

All inputs are as printed in the cited sources; results are rounded to the stated precision from unrounded arithmetic.

## Next module

The business and transaction module (CP-1A) follows. Carry forward: the Italian Lotto license (final installment of 1,675 paid April 24, 2026, amortized over nine years from December 2025, which drives the 323 LTM add-back) is the central financing and earnings-quality item; the consortium partners fund part of it through non-controlling interest capital increases (650 in H1 2026) and took 163 of cash distributions in H1 2026 (the same amount as in FY2025 and H1 2025); the sale of the gaming business on July 1, 2025 is the perimeter change behind all continuing-operations comparatives; and the UK contract transition in August 2025 reduces service revenue. The fundamental credit synthesis should use the leverage range of 3.24x on management's definition and 4.48x without the license-fee add-back, treat covenant headroom as unknown, and keep the August 4, 2026 evidence cut-off in view. The evidence trace validator should check the deck-derived Adjusted EBITDA figures against their locators.

### Business and transaction view

The business is a contracted, wager-linked lottery services company whose creditor-relevant features sit in four places. First, revenue visibility is high on paper, with about 92% of FY2025 revenue from long-term operating, facilities management and lottery management contracts, but U.S. contracts can be ended by the lottery authority at will with limited notice and the two Italian licenses together supplied about 37% of revenue. Second, the Italian licenses are the key transaction exposure: the new nine-year Lotto license cost an upfront fee of €2,230 million, paid in three installments ending April 24, 2026, and it is now amortized against revenue; the Scratch and Win license expires in September 2028. Third, control is concentrated in De Agostini with 63.28% of votes, and the documented behaviour since the sale of the gaming business on July 1, 2025 is debt reduction alongside large shareholder distributions, within term loan limits whose current text is not supplied. Fourth, the Italian Lotto structure shares cash flow with partners, so consolidated figures include cash that belongs partly to non-controlling interests. The evidence is adequate for a business-context fact pack, but the concession terms, the consortium agreements and any event after August 4, 2026 are not in the pack.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Sale of the gaming and digital business. On July 1, 2025 the company completed the sale of IGT Gaming to a holding company owned by funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management, pursuant to agreements entered into on July 26, 2024. The 20-F records total consideration, net of $134 million of cash and restricted cash transferred, of $4.1 billion and a pre-tax gain of $112 million (20-F page:156). The business is a discontinued operation, so every continuing-operations comparative excludes it. Continuing involvement is limited to licensing between the two groups, a 60.0% interest in Rhode Island VLT Company LLC whose economic benefits were transferred to IGT Gaming, and a guarantee of a lease of IGT Gaming that expires September 30, 2032 with maximum base-rent exposure of $94 million at June 30, 2026 (Q2 6-K page:17 and page:18). A receivable from the buyer of $21 million at June 30, 2026 will be collected through 2027 (Q2 6-K page:17). De Agostini retained an investment in the combined private company (20-F page:156); its size is not stated in the text read.

Use of proceeds. The filings state two uses. First, debt repayment: on the sale the company redeemed the 4.125% dollar notes due April 2026 and the 3.500% euro notes due June 2026 and prepaid euro term loan and revolver amounts, and the interim notes say $2 billion of debt was required to be repaid within six months of closing (20-F page:170; Q2 6-K page:17). Second, shareholder returns: the 20-F describes a "previously announced plan to return $1.1 billion of net cash proceeds from the IGT Gaming divestiture to shareholders" (20-F page:58). Execution documented in FY2025 includes a special dividend of $600 million (Q4 deck page:6, management claim), a $250 million accelerated share repurchase and a total of $770 million of cash dividends and $271 million of repurchases for the year (20-F page:123 and page:139).

Italian Lotto license. On July 16, 2025 the regulator notified that the consortium led by Brightstar had been awarded the Italian Lotto license for nine years from December 1, 2025. The upfront fee was €2,230 million, paid as €500 million on July 17, 2025, €300 million on November 28, 2025 and €1,430 million ($1,675 million) on April 24, 2026 (20-F page:163; Q2 6-K page:12). The Q1 deck states Brightstar's share of the final installment as €879 million or $1.03 billion (Q1 deck page:6, management claim); that share equals about 61.5% of €1,430 million, consistent with the stated ownership of Lottoitalia. Partners funded their share through non-controlling interest capital increases of $650 million in the first half of 2026 (Q2 6-K page:5). The license is amortized against revenue from December 2025 and the Q2 deck states that about $175 million of incremental Lotto-related service revenue amortization affects FY2026 reported growth (Q2 deck page:7, management claim).

New debt issues and refinancing. In September 2024 Brightstar Lottery Holdings B.V. issued €500 million of 4.250% notes at par (20-F page:170). In March 2025 the Parent and Brightstar Lottery S.p.A. entered into a facilities agreement for two €500 million term loans due September 2030, one used to repay revolver borrowings and one to fund the share of the Lotto fee (20-F page:171). In December 2025 the Parent and a subsidiary as co-issuers issued $750 million of 5.750% senior secured notes due January 2033 at par and used the proceeds and cash to redeem the $750 million 6.250% notes due January 2027 at 101.22%, with a $10 million loss on extinguishment (20-F page:169 and page:170). In March 2026 the company signed new senior secured revolving credit facilities of $650 million and €1.0 billion expiring March 2031, effective April 2026, cancelled both revolvers due July 2027 and amended the 2030 term loans to align provisions; in April 2026 it prepaid the remaining €200 million of the January 2027 term loan from revolver borrowings (Q2 6-K page:15). The June 30, 2026 principal is $4,383 million with the first maturity of $228 million in 2027 (see the financial base). Documented status of all items above: completed. No debt issuance is documented after June 30, 2026.

Subsequent events to the latest report: a dividend of $0.23 per share declared July 30, 2026, repurchases of $10 million to July 31, 2026, and the July 10, 2026 payment of a Mexican tax settlement (Q2 6-K page:17, page:18, page:19). Nothing after August 4, 2026 is supplied.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Brightstar has an adequate credit profile: contracted revenue and USD 1,742 million of liquidity support it, but net leverage of 3.24x rests on adjusted earnings, and Italian renewal risk in 2028 and partner claims limit headroom. | Medium | Covenant levels, license agreements and any reporting after August 4, 2026 are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Net leverage of 3.24x becomes 4.48x without the license-fee add-back in Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,170 million. | Leverage tolerance depends on a management measure, not a filed figure. | Medium |
| Liquidity of USD 1,742 million is 1.70x the 2027 and 2028 maturities of USD 1,026 million combined. | Near-term refinancing is covered; the 2028 to 2030 maturities are the wall. | High |

| Free cash flow excluding the Lotto payments was USD 387 million over the last twelve months, and partners took USD 163 million of distributions. | Debt reduction capacity after partners is moderate. | Medium |
| The Scratch and Win license expires in September 2028, beside USD 798 million of 2028 maturities. | Renewal terms could add funding pressure at the same time. | Low |
| De Agostini controls 63.28% of the votes. | Distribution policy sits with one holder, and the current distribution caps are not supplied. | Medium |
### Credit view

Brightstar Lottery PLC has an adequate fundamental credit profile with real near-term support but limited margin for error. The strongest support is contracted, wager-linked revenue, about 92% of FY2025 revenue, and liquidity of USD 1,742 million with no debt maturing before 2027, after the final USD 1,675 million Italian Lotto payment was absorbed. The weakest point is the quality of 3.24x net leverage: it uses management's Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back USD 323 million of license amortization and would read 4.48x without it, while partners and a controlling shareholder take part of the cash flow. The outcome depends on free cash flow after the investment cycle, the Scratch and Win renewal in September 2028 beside USD 798 million of 2028 maturities, and covenant terms that are not supplied.
### Key findings

Net leverage is acceptable on management's measure but weaker on a cash-oriented one. Net debt was USD 3,796 million at June 30, 2026 against last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,170 million, which is 3.24x, and total debt over the same EBITDA is 3.72x [financial base: leverage]. Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 323 million of license-fee amortization for the same period, and without that add-back net leverage is 4.48x [financial base: definition review]. The add-back relates to fees already paid in cash, which is why the reported figure is not unreasonable, but it means the leverage ratio flatters the cash burden of renewals in a business whose Italian licenses run for about nine years. The headline rise from 2.44x at December 31, 2025 to 3.24x mostly reflects the settlement of a USD 1,680 million regulator payable that sat outside debt; counting that payable, leverage at December 31, 2025 would have been 3.94x, so the like-for-like movement over six months was a decrease, helped by USD 650 million of partner capital contributions [financial base: claims outside debt; business context: Italian Lotto license].

Liquidity and maturities are comfortable for two years and heavier after that. Liquidity is USD 1,742 million, made of USD 558 million of cash and USD 1,185 million of undrawn revolver, against 2027 and 2028 principal maturities of USD 1,026 million combined, which is 1.70x cover [financial base: liquidity and maturities]. Total principal is USD 4,383 million, of which USD 2,883 million is in euros and all of it is senior secured, and the 2028 to 2030 maturities total USD 2,801 million, about 64% of principal. The new revolver runs to March 2031 with USD 604 million drawn. The risk is a concentrated refinancing window in 2028 to 2030 that coincides with the Scratch and Win renewal.

Cash generation is positive before license payments but is shared. Operating cash flow excluding Lotto payments was USD 761 million over the last twelve months and free cash flow excluding them USD 387 million; reported free cash flow was negative USD 2,214 million because of the USD 2,601 million of license payments in the period [financial base: financials]. Out of the USD 387 million, partners took USD 163 million of distributions, leaving USD 224 million for debt reduction and shareholders, and shareholder returns of USD 1,090 million over the same twelve months (including the USD 600 million special dividend funded from the sale of the gaming business) therefore came from sale proceeds and not from recurring cash flow [business context: ownership and governance]. In the first half of 2026 free cash flow excluding Lotto payments of USD 269 million less partner distributions of USD 163 million was USD 106 million, below the USD 130 million returned to shareholders. Capital expenditure of USD 190 million is expected in the second half of 2026 for new contracts.

The business has strong contractual visibility, concentrated in Italy and exposed to renewals. About 92% of revenue comes from long-term contracts, but the two Italian licenses supplied about 37% of FY2025 revenue and many U.S. contracts can be ended at will with limited notice [business context: operating model]. The Italian Lotto license runs to November 2034, while the Scratch and Win license expires in September 2028 and is not renewable unless its terms say so; the new Lotto license required an upfront fee of EUR 2,230 million. If a renewal needs a comparable upfront payment, it would arrive when USD 798 million of debt matures, a mechanic and not a forecast, since the renewal terms are not in the evidence.

Partners and the controlling shareholder claim part of the cash flow. The Italian Lotto manager is 61.5% owned by the company's Italian subsidiary, partners contributed USD 650 million of capital in the first half of 2026, and in FY2025 income attributable to non-controlling interests of USD 136 million exceeded total income from continuing operations of USD 135 million [business context: operating model]. De Agostini holds 46.29% of the shares and 63.28% of the votes, so distribution and leverage policy is its to set; the term loan agreements limited distributions at December 31, 2025, but the March 2026 amendment is not supplied.

What is not known matters. Covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom under the maximum net leverage and minimum interest coverage tests cannot be calculated even though the company reports compliance; nothing after August 4, 2026 is available; and ratings are known only at December 31, 2025 (BBB- from Fitch, Ba1 from Moody's, BB+ from S&P) [readiness; financial base: covenants].
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength: contracted, wager-linked revenue. About 92% of FY2025 revenue comes from long-term operating, facilities management and lottery management contracts with a revenue-weighted remaining term of 5.1 years for facilities management contracts and 5.6 years for the Italian licenses, so revenue is visible, and the company owns the technology and equipment it places, including more than 350,000 point-of-sale devices [business context: operating model]. Category: Documentary Fact.

Strength: liquidity and a staggered maturity profile. Liquidity of USD 1,742 million and no maturity before 2027 give two years of room, and the 2027 maturity of USD 228 million is small against that liquidity [financial base: liquidity and maturities]. Category: Documentary Fact.

Strength: deleveraging since the sale of the gaming business. Carrying debt fell from USD 5,361 million at December 31, 2024 to USD 4,178 million at December 31, 2025 and net leverage on management's measure from 4.08x to 2.44x before the Lotto payment, with refinancing already completed for 2026 [financial base: leverage; business context: transactions]. Category: Documentary Fact.
Strength: interest cover. Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 6.09x over the last twelve months, against 5.26x in FY2025 [financial base: interest cover]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

Weakness: leverage quality. Net leverage of 3.24x depends on management's measure that adds back USD 323 million of license amortization; without it leverage is 4.48x and cash interest cover is 4.41x [financial base: definition review]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

Weakness: Italian concentration and the 2028 renewal. The two Italian licenses are about 37% of revenue, the Scratch and Win license expires in September 2028, and the license assets pass to the State free of charge at expiry [business context: operating model]. Category: Documentary Fact.

Weakness: partner leakage and consolidated figures. Consolidated debt and EBITDA include 100% of the Italian joint venture while partners hold 38.5% of the Lotto manager and non-controlling interests took USD 163 million of distributions in the first half of 2026, so consolidated leverage does not isolate the claims of the parent's creditors on partner-owned cash [business context: operating model]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

Weakness: customer and jackpot exposure. The top ten customers outside Italy supplied about 35% of FY2025 revenue, a customer that contributed USD 37 million of FY2025 revenue left in August 2025, and lottery management incentives fell by USD 51 million in FY2025 on weak jackpot activity [business context: operating model]. Category: Documentary Fact.

Weakness: control and distributions. One holder controls the vote, shareholder returns have exceeded recurring free cash flow after partners, and creditor protection depends on distribution caps whose current text is not supplied [business context: ownership and governance]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.
### Credit assessment
| Dimension | Assessment | Category | Confidence | Basis and limitation |

| Business risk | Adequate to good visibility, with Italian and renewal concentration | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Financial base and business context; concession and consortium terms not supplied |

| Financial risk | Moderate to high leverage, 3.24x on management's measure and 4.48x without the license-fee add-back | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure; covenant EBITDA not supplied |
| Liquidity | Strong near term at USD 1,742 million; heavier maturities from 2028 | Documentary Fact | High | Letters of credit under the new revolver not stated |
| Cash flow quality | Positive before license payments, shared with partners | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Partner distributions are paid mainly in the first half; no second-half data |
| Governance and control | Controlled by one holder; no creditor-adverse action documented | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Indentures and the March 2026 amendment not supplied |

| Overall fundamental view | Adequate credit profile with limited headroom | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Below High because the business context records only conditional readiness for this module and high-severity gaps |
### Thesis

Brightstar's contracted lottery revenue and USD 1,742 million of liquidity support an adequate credit profile, but leverage quality, Italian renewal risk and partner and shareholder claims on cash flow limit headroom until the 2028 to 2030 refinancing window is addressed. Category: Analyst Interpretation.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| EBITDA quality | Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 323 million of license amortization tied to cash fees already paid | Leverage tolerance is overstated if renewals need new upfront fees; monitor cash-based leverage | Material |

| Italian license renewal | The Scratch and Win license expires in September 2028 and is not renewable unless its terms say so; the Lotto fee was EUR 2,230 million | Renewal funding could coincide with USD 798 million of 2028 maturities; refinancing risk | Material |

| Partner leakage | Partners hold 38.5% of the Lotto manager and non-controlling interests took USD 163 million of distributions in the first half of 2026 | Cash available for debt service is lower than consolidated EBITDA suggests | Material |
| Contract and customer loss | Many U.S. contracts terminate at will; top ten non-Italian customers are about 35% of revenue | Sudden revenue and EBITDA loss is possible; event risk | Material |

| Refinancing window | 2028, 2029 and 2030 principal of USD 2,801 million in total; revolver USD 604 million drawn to 2031 | Market access must be maintained in 2028 to 2030; liquidity covers 2027 and 2028 only | Material |

| Controlling shareholder policy | De Agostini controls 63.28% of votes; distributions exceeded recurring free cash flow after partners | Leverage tolerance and distributions are set by one holder; caps are the main protection | Material |

| Currency | USD 2,883 million of principal is in euros; euro moves changed the same term loan principal from USD 1,175 million to USD 1,139 million | Dollar leverage and debt move with the exchange rate without repayment | Minor |
| Covenant opacity | Covenants named but not quantified | Headroom cannot be monitored from filings | Material |
## Calculations

| Free cash flow excluding Lotto payments after partner distributions, last twelve months | 387 - 163 | USD 224 million |

| Shareholder returns, last twelve months | 774 + 316 | USD 1,090 million |
| Net debt change, December 31, 2025 to June 30, 2026 | 3,796 - 2,732 | USD 1,064 million, against the USD 1,675 million license payment and USD 650 million of partner capital contributions |
| Like-for-like leverage including the regulator payable | December 31, 2025: (2,732 + 1,680) / 1,121; June 30, 2026: 3,796 / 1,170 | 3.94x then 3.24x |

## Gaps

| Not supplied: any report after August 4, 2026, including third-quarter 2026 results | High | Leverage, liquidity and events after June 30, 2026 | Obtain the latest filing if published by 2026-11-05 |

The evidence trace validator (CP-5) follows. It should test that each figure here equals its handoff value, in particular 3.24x, 4.48x, USD 1,742 million, USD 1,026 million, USD 387 million, USD 224 million and 63.9%, and that the like-for-like leverage comparison (3.94x then 3.24x) rests on handoff figures; and it should confirm that no recovery conclusion, instrument recommendation or peer ranking appears.
